inputs.original_text: ISRAEL’S parliament began a debate today on a Bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. The Bill’s passage would be a victory for Israel’s far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of the religious party that introduced the legislation. Opponents of the legislation call it racist, draconian and unlikely to deter attacks by Palestinian militants.
inputs.modified_text: Israel’s parliament started a debate today on a Bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. Passing the Bill would be a victory for Israel’s far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir, who leads the religious party that introduced the legislation. Opponents of the legislation describe it as racist, draconian, and unlikely to deter attacks by Palestinian militants.
